mitigation_mechanism: Reforestation slows storm runoff and lowers flood peaks in catchment models: in Slovakia's Hornad watershed a 50% increase of forest cut a simulated flood peak from 84.8 to 74.9 m3/s and reduced peaks by about 24% on average in rain-duration tests, more for short storms than long ones [ev_flood_hazard_bahremand06_1, ev_flood_hazard_bahremand06_3], and an afforestation simulation for Luxembourg's Alzette basin decreased the peak by 8% [ev_flood_hazard_bahremand06_5]. WOCAT compilers for area closures in Ethiopia, afforestation in Eritrea, Cabo Verde and Bosnia and Herzegovina, floodplain reafforestation in Tajikistan and a learning site in Afghanistan rate downstream flooding or flood impacts as reduced; an Ethiopian compiler notes that runoff from the watershed is highly reduced, and the Afghan compiler that riverbanks were revegetated with communities planting cuttings along banks and shorelines [ev_flood_hazard_wocat_1072_2011_downstream_flooding, ev_flood_hazard_wocat_1048_2011_downstream_flooding, ev_flood_hazard_wocat_1330_2010_downstream_flooding, ev_flood_hazard_wocat_1509_2011_flood_impacts, ev_flood_hazard_wocat_7460_2024_flood_impacts].

mitigation_mechanism: This row describes the flood regulation that standing forest provides and that protection keeps. A country-level analysis of developing countries predicted that a further hypothetical 10% loss of natural forest cover would raise flood frequency by 3.5% to 28.1% and flood duration by 3.8% to 7.9% [ev_flood_hazard_bradshaw07_1, ev_flood_hazard_bradshaw07_2]. At the local scale forests and forest soils reduce runoff through enhanced infiltration and storage, and peak flows rise after forest removal in small experimental catchments [ev_flood_hazard_faocifor05_1, ev_flood_hazard_vandijk09_2]. In Malaysia an analysis with adequate controls for confounding factors found flood risk increased after natural forest was converted to plantation crops and urban land [ev_flood_hazard_iufro18_1], in the USA forest harvest was associated with significant increases in peak flows in both small and large (100 - 1,000 km2) basins [ev_flood_hazard_iufro18_3], and in Swiss valleys with more than 30% forest snowmelt was more gradual and flooding risk lower [ev_flood_hazard_iufro18_2]. At a learning site in Afghanistan the compiler rates flood impacts as decreased after riverbanks were revegetated through control measures [ev_flood_hazard_wocat_7460_2024_flood_impacts].
caveats: The service fades with storm size and basin size. Forest soils reduce runoff only in small-scale rainfall events, which are not responsible for severe downstream flooding, and forests cannot stop catastrophic large-scale floods caused by severe meteorological events [ev_flood_hazard_faocifor05_1, ev_flood_hazard_faocifor05_2]; small to medium peak flows are affected most while the largest events do not change noticeably, and studies in larger basins have not usually found changes after deforestation of up to 50% of the catchment [ev_flood_hazard_vandijk09_3, ev_flood_hazard_vandijk09_4]; and in the Himalaya tree cutting was not the reason for flooding in the downstream plains [ev_flood_hazard_iufro18_4]. The cross-country analysis itself found little evidence that further forest loss changed flood deaths or damage [ev_flood_hazard_bradshaw07_3, ev_flood_hazard_bradshaw07_4], and a reanalysis of its data found the correlation between forest cover or cover loss and flood frequency appears absent, with the degraded-lands fraction accounting for most of the variation [ev_flood_hazard_vandijk09_1]. The literature is contested: the two country-level statistical analyses disagree, the FAO–CIFOR and van Dijk statements are expert syntheses, the Malaysian, US and Swiss results are secondary citations in a global assessment, and all compare forest with cleared or less-forested land, so they show what losing forest costs rather than the outcome of a protection or community forestry programme. The Afghanistan unit is a practitioner rating from a learning site that bundles several land and forest management practices [ev_flood_hazard_wocat_7460_2024_flood_impacts].
